newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dollar pauses after soaring on Bonn-Buba row.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dollar pauses after soaring on Bonn-Buba row.

text.p: The dollar on Thursday paused in its strong surge against the mark triggered by a row between Germany and its central bank that has renewed anxieties about Europe's planned single currency.

In equities, Paris stocks dipped after a strong morning rally seemed to have halted this week's big losses caused by fears that the left may be well placed for Sunday's runoff parliamentary elections. Elsewhere, London put on a shaky performance.

Most of the excitement was in currency markets where the dollar climbed nearly two pfennigs to 1.7067 marks, boosted by its reputation as a shelter in uncertain times after Germany's central bank denounced government plans to revalue its gold reserves.
"If you are talking about safe-haven currencies, then sterling and the dollar spring to mind," said Stuart Frost, analyst at NatWest Markets.
But by early afternoon the dollar had eased back to 1.6970, as against 1.6905 in late Europe on Wednesday, after German Finance Minister Theo Waigel elaborated on his revaluation plans.
He said said his intention to revalue the Bundesbank's gold reserves remained necessary despite the central bank's strong objection to the plan.

Waigel told journalists that "not a single mark from a revaluation of the reserve stock would be funneled" into Bonn's budget, which critics have said would help ready Germany for entry into Europe's currency union.
The Bundesbank's harsh attack on the government, which aimed to use the revaluation to ease long-term debt, sent jitters through the market in the run-up to European Monetary Union.
The public rift in Germany has added spice to EMU uncertainty in Europe as it follows an unexpectedly strong showing for the Socialists in France's parliamentary elections.

Market expectations are that if the Socialists are elected during the final run-off this weekend, they will push for Italy and Spain to be included among EMU's founding members -- watering down the euro from the start.

"The dollar should be favoured against the deutschmark because of the French elections and because the gold-revaluation rift has given a blow to Germany's reputation," said Claudio Demolli, foreign exchange strategist at Merrill Lynch.
The gold plan will also make it difficult for Germany to reject countries such as Spain and Italy joining the first round of monetary union in 1999.
Against the yen, the dollar got a boost from an unexpected fall in Japan's April industrial production, which dampened expectations of higher Japanese rates.

In equity markets, Paris soared by more than one percent at one point after closing down 3.63 percent on Wednesday -- the second big drop of the week prompted by the enhanced prospects for the left in elections on Sunday.
But the market lost early gains and slipped into the minus column in the afternoon, buffeted by rumours of conflicting private opinion polls about Sunday's election runoff.
The share market has fallen more than six percent over the last three days as investors have taken more seriously the prospect of a left-wing win in the election.

The bourse see-sawed on Thursday after a California-based internet site published three polls which indicated the left was well placed, while a Swiss-based French language paper was set to publish a poll on Thursday evening rumoured to indicate the opposite.
"It's a market of excesses. There have been enormous swings but they do not mean much. On top of that, the dollar is up and the international situation is not bad," a broker said.
In London, stocks recovered after making a negative start, hit by the new uncertainty over EMU. By early afternoon and after a poor opening on Wall Street, the shares were barely showing a profit.
"The market is around its highs and when you get wobbles like these around Europe, the market's not too happy," said BZW strategist Steve Wright.
Sterling strengthened against the mark, a factor which has squeezed profits warnings out of UK industry recently and driven share prices down.
"Sterling is back up at 2.79 (against the mark) and that's not going to help," said a dealer at one point.
In Frankfurt, floor trade was closed because of a public holiday. Dealings on the electronic IBIS index made small gains, encouraged by the stronger dollar and shrugging off the Bonn-Buba clash.
"The market is holding on rather well," said Birgit Bachmann at BHF Bank in Frankfurt. "I think the market has reacted so far relatively positively to the fight."
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6970 marks and 116.03 yen compared with 1.6902 marks and 115.86 yen in late European trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 0.8 points at 4,678.3
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 14.68 points at 2,568.48.
FRANKFURT - The German bourse was closed for floor trade. In screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index was up 9.76 points at 3636.36.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $343.90 an ounce, compared with Wednesday's close of $345.05 in London. Silver was three cents stronger at $4.75.
